category: More phrasal verbs on irregular bases: A-L

entries.meaning: To push the price of something higher by making one offer after another for it. ---
examples: Collectors are bidding up anything that comes out of that studio.
Two rival funds bid the stock up forty percent in a single week.
Rumors of a shortage have bid up the price of copper.
entries.русский: взвинчивать цену, взвинтить цену; набавлять ставку, набавить ставку
entries.separable: separable — bid up the price, and with a pronoun it must split, bid it up
entries.forms: bid up · bid up · bid up

entries.meaning: To arrive somewhere suddenly and without warning. ---
examples: He blows into town twice a year and expects everyone to drop everything.
She blew into the office an hour late, still holding her coat.
A cousin I had never met had blown into town the night before.
entries.русский: нагрянуть, заявиться; внезапно приезжать, внезапно приехать
entries.separable: inseparable — blow into town, never ✗ blow town into
entries.forms: blow into · blew into · blown into

entries.meaning: To carry or take someone or something to the place where the other person is. ---
examples: Bring over whatever you were planning to cook.
She brought her new boyfriend over on Sunday.
They have brought over half their furniture already.
entries.русский: приносить, принести; привозить, привезти; приводить, привести (к кому-л.)
entries.separable: separable — bring over a chair, and with a pronoun it must split, bring it over
entries.forms: bring over · brought over · brought over

entries.meaning: To persuade someone to accept your opinion or join your side. ---
examples: Two more speeches might bring over the delegates who are still undecided.
The pay offer brought three of the holdouts over.
By Friday he had brought over even his loudest critics.
entries.русский: переманивать, переманить; склонять на свою сторону, склонить на свою сторону
entries.separable: separable — bring over the undecided voters, and with a pronoun it must split, bring them over
entries.forms: bring over · brought over · brought over

entries.meaning: To admit you were wrong and give up a demand or a claim you had insisted on. ---
examples: Neither side wants to climb down first.
The company climbed down and paid the refunds.
They have climbed down from every threat they made.
entries.русский: отступать, отступить (от требований); идти на попятную, пойти на попятную
entries.separable: no object — what is given up arrives through from: climb down from that demand
entries.forms: climb down · climbed down · climbed down

entries.meaning: To move down from a high place, holding on with your hands and feet. ---
examples: Hold the rails while you climb down.
He climbed down the fire escape in his socks.
She was climbing down from the hayloft when the ladder slipped.
entries.русский: слезать, слезть; спускаться, спуститься
entries.separable: inseparable — climb down the ladder, never ✗ climb the ladder down
entries.forms: climb down · climbed down · climbed down
entries.transitivity: both — intransitive (climb down slowly), transitive (climb down the ladder)

entries.meaning: To be the result of something. ---
examples: Nothing good comes of arguing with him.
Whatever came of that job offer in Denver?
Nothing has come of the complaint we filed.
entries.русский: выходить, выйти (из чего-л.); получаться, получиться в результате
entries.separable: inseparable — come of the meeting, never ✗ come the meeting of
entries.forms: come of · came of · come of

entries.meaning: To remove liquid from a container or from the body by letting it flow out. ---
examples: Draw off the fat before you make the gravy.
The surgeon drew a liter of fluid off the lung.
Once the water has been drawn off, the tank can be scrubbed.
entries.русский: сливать, слить; отводить, отвести (жидкость); откачивать, откачать
entries.separable: separable — draw off the liquid, and with a pronoun it must split, draw it off
entries.forms: draw off · drew off · drawn off

entries.meaning: Of ground, to slope sharply downward from where you are standing. ---
examples: Behind the cabin the hillside falls away into a ravine.
The path fell away so steeply that we went down on all fours.
We stood where the ground had fallen away to a beach two hundred feet below.
entries.русский: круто спускаться, круто уходить вниз (о местности)
entries.separable: no object — the hillside falls away, never ✗ fall the hillside away
entries.forms: fall away · fell away · fallen away

entries.meaning: To become steadily fewer, weaker, or less until almost nothing is left. ---
examples: Attendance always falls away after the holidays.
Her support in the polls fell away week by week.
By March most of the volunteers had fallen away.
entries.русский: убывать, убыть; таять, растаять (о поддержке); сходить на нет, сойти на нет
entries.separable: no object — support fell away, never ✗ fall the support away
entries.forms: fall away · fell away · fallen away

entries.meaning: To topple from an upright position to the ground. ---
examples: The vase fell over when the door slammed.
Careful — that stack of books is going to fall over.
She had fallen over twice on the ice before she gave up.
entries.русский: падать, упасть; опрокидываться, опрокинуться
entries.separable: inseparable — fall over the cord, never ✗ fall the cord over
entries.forms: fall over · fell over · fallen over
entries.transitivity: both — intransitive (the lamp fell over), transitive (he fell over the cord)

entries.meaning: To become someone's duty or responsibility, usually because no one else will do it. ---
examples: Delivering bad news always falls to the manager.
It fell to me to tell the family.
Every unpleasant chore in this office has fallen to her.
entries.русский: выпадать на долю, выпасть на долю; доставаться, достаться (об обязанности)
entries.separable: inseparable — it fell to me, never ✗ fall me to
entries.forms: fall to · fell to · fallen to

entries.meaning: To move from place to place, especially when age or injury makes it hard. ---
examples: At ninety she still gets about without a cane.
After the surgery he got about on crutches for a month.
She has gotten about much better since the new knee.
entries.русский: передвигаться, перемещаться (особ. с трудом); выходить из дома
entries.separable: no object — get about on crutches, never ✗ get the crutches about
entries.forms: get about · got about · gotten about

entries.meaning: To find out about someone's secret or dishonest activity. ---
examples: It takes the auditors years to get onto a scheme like that.
The police got onto him through a tip from a neighbor.
By then the IRS had gotten onto the whole operation.
entries.русский: выходить на след, выйти на след; раскусить, разоблачить
entries.separable: inseparable — get onto the scheme, never ✗ get the scheme onto
entries.forms: get onto · got onto · gotten onto

entries.meaning: To start talking about a particular subject, often by drifting there. ---
examples: Whatever you do, don't get onto the subject of his divorce.
Somehow we got onto the war, and dinner was ruined.
Once he has gotten onto baseball, there is no stopping him.
entries.русский: переходить, перейти (к теме); заговаривать, заговорить (о чём-л.)
entries.separable: inseparable — get onto politics, never ✗ get politics onto
entries.forms: get onto · got onto · gotten onto

entries.meaning: To find a way past a rule, an obstacle, or a difficulty without meeting it head-on. ---
examples: There is no way to get round the residency requirement.
They got round the ban by renaming the product.
Every firm in town has gotten round that tax somehow.
entries.русский: обходить, обойти (правило, препятствие)
entries.separable: inseparable — get round the rule, never ✗ get the rule round
entries.forms: get round · got round · gotten round

entries.meaning: To look, taste, or work well in combination. ---
examples: Those two colors do not go together.
Nobody thought red wine and fish went together until that dinner.
Hard work and luck have always gone together in his telling of it.
entries.русский: сочетаться, подходить друг к другу; гармонировать
entries.separable: no object — the colors go together, never ✗ go the colors together
entries.forms: go together · went together · gone together

entries.meaning: To stay in a place doing nothing in particular. ---
examples: Teenagers hang about the parking lot until the store closes.
We hung about for an hour and then gave up.
He has hung about that bar every night since he lost the job.
entries.русский: слоняться, околачиваться; торчать (где-л.)
entries.separable: inseparable — hang about the station, never ✗ hang the station about
entries.forms: hang about · hung about · hung about
entries.transitivity: both — intransitive (stop hanging about), transitive (hang about the lobby)

entries.meaning: To keep a feeling from showing or escaping. ---
examples: Don't hold in your anger until it explodes.
She held her tears in until the door closed behind her.
He has held in so much resentment that it comes out sideways.
entries.русский: сдерживать, сдержать (чувства); подавлять, подавить
entries.separable: separable — hold in your anger, and with a pronoun it must split, hold it in
entries.forms: hold in · held in · held in

entries.meaning: To put your body flat on a surface in order to rest. ---
examples: Go lie down for an hour and see if the headache passes.
She lay down on the couch and was asleep in a minute.
The dog had lain down right across the doorway.
entries.русский: ложиться, лечь; прилечь, полежать
entries.separable: no object — nothing ever comes between lie and down; where and how long follow after: lie down on the couch, lie down for an hour
entries.forms: lie down · lay down · lain down

entries.meaning: To attack someone suddenly with angry words or with blows.
examples: My father lit into me for coming home at two in the morning.
She'll light into anybody who criticizes her kids.
He had lit into the referee before we could pull him away.
entries.русский: набрасываться, наброситься (на кого-л.); отчитывать, отчитать; накидываться
entries.separable: inseparable — the person follows into: light into him, light into the coach; never ✗ light him into
entries.forms: light into · lit into · lit into
